message.content:
I’m sorry—I don’t have access to live clocks or an up‑to‑date world‑time database, so I can’t tell you the exact current local time in New York City right now.

If you need the present time there, here’s what you can do:

| Option | How it works |
|--------|--------------|
| **Phone/Computer Clock** | Most devices automatically adjust to your timezone if they’re set to “automatic” or “network‑based.” Just look at the clock on your phone, laptop, or desktop. |
| **Web Search** | Type “current time in New York” into Google (or another search engine) – the result box will show the correct local time. |
| **World Clock Apps/Websites** | Use services like TimeandDate.com, WorldTimeBuddy, or built‑in world‑clock widgets on iOS/Android. |

A quick reminder about daylight saving:
* Standard time (Eastern Standard Time, EST): UTC−5  
* Daylight Saving Time (Eastern Daylight Time, EDT): UTC−4  

The switch usually happens on the second Sunday in March (clocks move forward one hour) and reverts on the first Sunday in November (clocks move back). If you know whether those dates apply today, you can manually subtract either 4 or 5 hours from Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) to get the local time.
